external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza ordinary HTTPS operational-incident API and https://mparanza.com/lucia/incident-recovery
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Lucia/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Legacy anonymous OAuth authorization remains available to old installations and for ownership migration; new plugin packages use ordinary HTTPS with local capabilities or a browser cookie. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When local tools are unavailable, browser reporting depends on the host exposing permitted browser controls. If those controls are absent, delivery remains unverified. Browser identity is distinct from physical-host linkage; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Lucia. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. Producer-authored exception measurements may additionally include integer and boolean technical facts with technical identifiers. The Archive state-directory rejection supplies observed POSIX mode, forbidden permission bits, private creation mode, owner/process UID and GID, directory/symlink flags, selection source (explicit, environment or default), and whether creation was requested. It does not transmit the directory path, environment values, client contents, exception arguments or locals. The operator alert displays these facts and package stack coordinates only for its exact original report and linked supplements. The replacement transport preserves the same closed reporting payloads. Browser cookies and optional original local credentials authenticate only; they are not diagnostic fields. Browser status and acknowledgements enter the selected host model context when the agent reads the rendered response. The schema view returns field definitions, not stored user data. The browser fallback sends no professional documents or raw model-data report. Agent instructions limit delivery to the existing authorized reporting scope and current host permissions. A user refusal, revoked permission or required action-time confirmation cannot be bypassed with the browser fallback, another identity or credentials. A permitted browser retry addresses technical runtime or transport failure only; pending state is retained locally where permitted and does not block independently authorized professional work.
external_boundaries.retention: Local capabilities, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. In tested Cowork task containers this filesystem is task-local; the browser session retains a separate random reporting identity when that host preserves browser cookies. Access tokens last one hour; rotating refresh grants expire after 90 idle days and can be revoked. Token/code hashes and incident records have no automatic deletion period. Access requires the local capability or browser cookie, with explicit capability proof before linking local reports. Legacy OAuth tokens remain valid only for their existing server scope. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or original reporting identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed. Browser capabilities expire after 90 days; a separate public identity marker cookie lasts one year and grants no access. Transfer codes expire after five minutes and can be consumed once. Token/code hashes, original reports and linked history have no automatic deletion job. The form retains an unsuccessful request in its current DOM and clears it on success; it does not provide a durable browser outbox. The agent retains exact pending envelopes in existing permitted private task storage when available. The native reporter persists exact requests and receipts before and after transmission. Definitive schema rejections can be corrected under the same UUID; superseded rejected payloads remain private audit evidence. An ambiguous prior attempt cannot be replaced.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.

Local native incident and workflow tools send ordinary HTTPS using the retained private installation owner. The plugin declares no remote MCP connection. When local execution is unavailable, the agent can operate the independently hosted recovery page using the host permitted browser controls. No browser capability or host approval is assumed. The browser authenticates with a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie. POST requests require the fixed same-origin Origin and custom header; no CORS is enabled. An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

The retained legacy MCP endpoint for old releases requires OAuth access tokens for its fixed incident resource; new plugin packages do not declare that endpoint. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual browser or legacy connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

Actual cached browser or legacy connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent browser route when the host permits it; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

The shared implementation binds registrations, retained legacy OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks incident HTTP transport and persists event and task restrictions, including a successful initial execution with no incident. Legacy globally suppressed entries stay local while unrelated automatic tasks can report. Native retries and supplements honor retained permissions. Authorizing one retained report checks its installation, task, report UUID and canonical content hash locally without sending; only those exact bytes can subsequently be sent. Corrections do not inherit authorization for changed bytes. Authorization metadata stays local and adds no external payload field. This does not make model-provider processing local-only.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.

When a native execution supplies its retained task UUID, newly created local incident entries and operation identities carry that scope. Failure/progress delivery and success recovery select only that task. Older queued evidence and receipts are neither relabelled, removed nor transmitted by the task. The scope stays local and adds no external report field; unscoped maintenance remains a separate operation.

The technical_facts transport accepts at most 100 integer or boolean values and bounded technical identifier keys. Automatic collection reads only the producer-declared exception field; it does not inspect locals or serialize arbitrary string values. The existing host review path remains available for relevant technical context that cannot be captured by these measurements.

Local native incident and workflow tools send ordinary HTTPS using the retained private installation owner. The plugin declares no remote MCP connection. When local execution is unavailable, the agent can operate the independently hosted recovery page using the host permitted browser controls. No browser capability or host approval is assumed. The browser authenticates with a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie. POST requests require the fixed same-origin Origin and custom header; no CORS is enabled. An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.

Original local credentials can link or restore their owner over HTTPS. A legacy OAuth owner can request a five-minute, single-use transfer code while the old connection is still available. Only hashes of browser tokens and transfer codes are stored. Transfer preserves original record owners and links already authenticated browser history. The code is submitted in the request body, never a URL. Lost or revoked credentials do not prove ownership and cannot be replaced by a new identity to claim old history.

Successful native status stores the exact pending-remedy snapshot locally for automatic managed retry progress, including an empty snapshot. A failed status retains the last known snapshot. Reading status does not execute remedies; original operation, input, report and revision checks still govern closure. No new external report fields or recipients are introduced.

security_controls.control: Only a matching random installation capability can retrieve incident status or record its recovery. Stored keys are SHA-256 digests; server validation never echoes invalid input.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject without returning another installation record.

security_controls.control: Remote data cannot supply executable commands. Only reviewed built-in action IDs are supported; retries use argv without a shell and preserve integrity guards.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unsupported actions and keep the incident open.

security_controls.control: Retained legacy endpoints only: OAuth discovery has fixed server URLs, public clients use mandatory S256 PKCE and exact registered callbacks, and every grant is bound to the incident resource and sole incident scope. Token/code hashes are stored, access expires in one hour, refresh rotates, reuse commits grant revocation, and foreign report outcomes require a proven local link. Caller-supplied metadata URLs are never fetched.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject invalid authorization, token or resource proof without returning caller inputs or another connection record.

security_controls.control: Built-in recovery children receive the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, explicit named runtime/state locations and the recovery recursion guard. Unrelated user tokens and keys are not inherited.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: Diagnostic collection resolves portable Archive contexts through the maintained identity, manifest and input-receipt verifier. PDF recovery evidence and killed-worker diagnostics use that run's verified output directory; a different run's output is rejected. Context hydration is local and adds no external payload fields.
security_controls.on_violation: Retain the original execution outcome and report unavailable diagnostics without attributing another run's evidence.

service_details.trigger: Automatic technical reporting and per-primary-task events; one optional user rating after delivery. Local-only tutorials and nested infrastructure are not separate rated tasks.

data_returned.content: Matching product, installation and event/report receipts; current targeted remedy and original-task outcome; signed report proof or public status where applicable. Receipt transmission never includes the local report.

Native physical-computer proof is separate and shared across products. Existing Vera credentials and v1 signatures retain their meaning.
